svg.text: One Databricks App in front of governed data, Genie and AI models. Every back-end call runs as the app’s own service principal; people never touch the data.
Consumer access + CAN_USE on the app (or
Stop) and read on the app code
One HTTPS address per app; one port
Databricks App · Node.js + AppKit · one port
public/ · HTML, JavaScript, CSS · runs in the browser
Then: follow-up suggestions · trace + usage log · streamed to the browser as server-sent events
App identity: the app’s service principal
Reads gold (SELECT) · runs Genie (CAN_RUN) · queries models (CAN_QUERY) · uses Lakebase
· stops itself (CAN_MANAGE on its own app) · no keys in code
Genie space: LensS MLOps Analytics (query engine)
Natural language → SQL over 16 governed sources. Defined in code:
instructions with the rule values written in, 25 example queries, 11
Llama 3.3 70B: router, guardrails, follow-ups, platform guide, memory ·
GPT-OSS 120B: answer judge · GTE Large: embeddings for the semantic cache.
chatapp schema: sessions, messages, usage & audit log, answer cache, cache
Runs Genie’s SQL and the app’s Command Center, Explorer and cost queries.
Governed data: gold certified views, metric views and business rules; plus
system.billing / system.query behind the cost view.
raw tables, as received; row counts checked
ONE-COMMAND DEPLOY (deploy/deploy.py → Databricks CLI, everything as code)
app step: creates or updates the app, binds Genie, warehouse, Lakebase and models; grants the service principal its access; gives readers CAN_USE and demo givers CAN_MANAGE;
shares the app code folder with those who can start it; creates the cost view; checks page scripts; syncs the code and deploys. smoke, routing and the org tests run only when asked.
Versions run side by side (e.g. v1: own app, schemas, Genie space, chat database); Observability shows cost per project, all versions counted as one.
